npl.citation: Yang TH, Cheng YW, Wang YT, Huang TW, Kang CW, Pan CT, Kuo HY, Chung CH, Chen CC, Liao YS (2023). "Assessment of hyperspectral imaging and CycleGAN-simulated narrowband techniques to detect early esophageal cancer." Scientific Reports (Nature) 13:20502. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-023-47833-y — SAVE HSI engine (Hitspectra Intelligent Technology, Kaohsiung, Taiwan) reconstructing hyperspectral imaging from standard RGB endoscopic video; CycleGAN narrowband imaging simulation; real-time \~25 fps; clinically superior early esophageal cancer inference vs conventional white-light imaging; validates HSI reconstruction from standard cameras for medical tissue inference in peer-reviewed clinical context

Hitspectra Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. (Kaohsiung, Taiwan). "Medicine — Guiding machine vision with hyperspectral images." [hitspectra.com/en/application.php?CNo=1](http://hitspectra.com/en/application.php?CNo=1) — Commercial HSI integration with standard medical lenses: dermatoscope (85% accuracy for skin pigment and haemoglobin abnormalities), ophthalmoscope (fundus layer analysis for retinal disease, glaucoma, optic nerve pathology), odontoscope (oral cancer staging, accuracy expected to reach 99.9%); SAVE HSI engine expanding 400+ analysable spectral channels from a single pixel of standard camera input; AI-assisted pathological image analysis; non-invasive disease identification without biopsy. All applications target tissue morphology via specialised medical lens hardware — not gene expression, not consumer smartphone cameras, not mental health
